body.name: \(\mathcal N_n(q_e)\)
body.construction: Let \(G_n=\{j/(64n^2):j=0,\ldots,n^2\}\). For \(q_e\in G_n\), define \[\mathcal N_n(q_e)=\left\{\nu=\sum_{\ell=1}^K w_\ell\delta_{u_\ell}:1\le K\le5,\ u_\ell\in H_n,\ w_\ell\in W_n,\ w_\ell\ge0,\ \sum_{\ell=1}^K w_\ell=1,\ \sum_{\ell=1}^K w_\ell u_\ell=0,\ \sum_{\ell=1}^K w_\ell u_\ell^2=q_e^2\right\}.\] This is a finite family. For every \(q_e\in G_n\), the law \(\nu=(\delta_{-q_e}+\delta_{q_e})/2\) belongs to \(\mathcal N_n(q_e)\), because \(\pm q_e\in H_n\) and \(1/2\in W_n\); its moments are \((q_e^2,0,q_e^4)\). At \(q_e=0\), the one-atom law \(\delta_0\) is also included.
